title: Introduction to CSS
description: How one CSS rule picks elements with a selector and changes them with a declaration.
congratsText: You can read and write a CSS rule!
objectives: Write a CSS rule inside a style block
Predict which elements a selector will change
Diagnose a broken declaration when the browser shows no error
Apply the rule shape to write a new rule with two declarations
recap: A rule is a selector, then braces with property: value; inside, in a style block in head.
The selector picks the elements; one rule changes every element it matches.
A missing colon breaks a declaration, and the browser skips it with no error.
Every rule shares one shape: selector, braces, and one declaration per line.

chunks.text: CSS changes how a page looks. In this lab, every rule goes inside a <style> block, inside head, right below title.

check.question: Where did the style block go in the lab?

chunks.text: A rule starts with a selector. The selector picks the elements. In p { color: red; }, the selector is p.

check.question: In p { color: red; }, what is the selector?

chunks.text: Inside the braces is the declaration: the declaration says what changes. It is a property, a colon, a value, and a semicolon: color: red;

check.question: What separates the property from the value?

quiz.question: Which part of this rule picks the elements to change?

chunks.text: The page has two paragraphs. After p { color: red; }, both turn red. One rule changes every element its selector matches.

check.question: How many paragraphs did the p rule turn red?

chunks.text: Elements the selector does not match keep their normal look. The h1 and the list items stayed black.

check.question: Why did the heading stay black?

chunks.text: Change the selector and you change what gets picked. A copy with li as the selector turns the list items red too.

check.question: What picked the list items in Experiment 3?

quiz.question: How many lines of text on this page turn red? Type a number.

chunks.text: In Experiment 2 you deleted one colon: color red;. The paragraphs went back to black.

check.question: What did deleting the colon do to the paragraphs?

chunks.text: The browser showed no error message. When it cannot read a declaration, it skips it and goes on.

check.question: Did the browser print an error on the page?

chunks.text: So when a rule seems to do nothing, check the small marks first: the colon, the semicolon, and the braces.

check.question: A rule does nothing. What do you check first?

quiz.question: The broken declaration was color red; — arrange the pieces to fix it.

chunks.text: A rule can hold more than one declaration. Your h1 rule has two: color: blue; and font-size: 40px;

check.question: How many declarations are in your h1 rule?

chunks.text: Each declaration ends with its own semicolon. Put each one on its own line so a missing mark is easy to spot.

check.question: Does each declaration need its own semicolon?

chunks.text: Every rule has the same shape: a selector, then braces, then property: value; inside. Only the words change.

check.question: What stays the same in every rule?

quiz.question: Which text on this page turns green?
options: Only the one paragraph on the page
The paragraph and both list items
